settings.quote: We wanted clothing that carries something — the twelve stones of the Choshen, and the faces of the tzadikim who came before us.

settings.heading: Twelve tribes, read in stone and color.
settings.text: The Choshen Collection takes the high priest's breastplate as its color card. Twelve pieces, one for each tribe, each garment-dyed to its own stone — odem for Yehuda, sapir for Levi, yashfeh for Binyamin — with the tribe's mark embroidered small and low.

settings.placeholder_caption: Tzadik Him — portrait drawing on press
settings.heading: The faces we keep close.
settings.text: Tzadik Him puts hand-drawn portraits of the tzadikim on heavyweight cotton — tees, crewnecks, hoodies. Each portrait is drawn in the studio, printed in small runs, and treated with the weight it deserves: no slogans, no noise, just the face.

settings.heading: Stay Close to Lyons of Judah
settings.text: New collections, atelier notes, and early access — quietly, in your inbox.
